subject: CPRA annex: emergency subprocessor activation + telemetry pseudonymization guarantee
messages:
From: Karen Holt <karen.holt@bluemarblehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BlueMarble Legal <data-privacy@bluemarblehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: telemetry fallback subprocessors — CPRA/annex questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the low-latency routing. We're spinning up a controlled pilot that will route hashed telemetry to a Redwood fallback processor for short-term analytic bursts. Legal asked we confirm two things before we sign the CPRA annex: 1) a short, auditable list of any temporary/ emergency subprocessors you might activate, and 2) a clear statement that telemetry will be pseudonymized such that it is not "personal information" under CCPA/CPRA sale definitions and won't be sold.

Could you send a draft annex we can review and a current subprocessor inventory? We have an internal timeline: procurement needs final language by EOD Wednesday (2027-09-15) to keep the pilot on schedule.

Also: will you accept a limited emergency activation clause that allows you to onboard short-term vendors (e.g., CDN/edge analytics) under defined criteria and notify us within 48 hours? If so, please include the notification process (who gets CC'd, what evidence is provided).

Attachments: BlueMarble_Qs.pdf (list of pilot scenarios)

Thanks,
Karen
Karen Holt
Director, Product Operations
BlueMarble Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karen Holt <karen.holt@bluemarblehealth.com>
Cc: BlueMarble Legal <data-privacy@bluemarblehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: telemetry fallback subprocessors — CPRA/annex questions

Hi Karen —

Appreciate the context and the timeline. I've attached a working draft of a CPRA annex that addresses emergency/temporary subprocessors and an extract of the current subprocessor inventory. High level:

- Pseudonymization: telemetry fields we receive for the pilot (session id, hashed user token, route metrics) will be pseudonymized at collection and stored using envelope encryption with customer-specific KMS keys. We include a short definitional block in the annex that states pseudonymized telemetry is not "personal information" for the purpose of sale, plus an audited mapping procedure in Exhibit B.

- Emergency activation: Redwood can activate short-term subprocessors for emergency capacity or maintenance (examples: edge analytics, transient CDN cache) under a defined checklist: SOC 2 Type II proof or equivalent within 72 hours, contractual attestation to the CPRA annex language, access-limited credentials, deletion within 30 days post-activation unless otherwise agreed. Notification to the customer and to legal (details below) within 48 hours is included.

- Notification process (draft): email to procurement and legal (addresses in your RFI), a one-page activation summary, and a link to the transient subprocessor's SOC evidence. We propose a 48-hour notice window plus a 5-business-day follow-up report.

Attachments: CPRA_Annex_Draft_v3.docx; subprocessor_list_2027-09-11.csv

I'm happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through the redlines before procurement reviews.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Strategic Accounts — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot: telemetry fallback subprocessors — CPRA/annex questions

Looping Neha in for legal signoff. Quick internal notes from product/sales POV:

- BlueMarble is sensitive to "sale" language. Rachel's pseudonymization description is good but procurement will likely push for an explicit "non-sale" covenant that survives termination for 12 months. Can legal accept that?

- The emergency activation checklist sounds heavy (SOC within 72 hours). Can we offer an alternative: for certain low-risk edge caches we accept a self-attestation with post-hoc SOC or audit within 30 days? That would make operational work easier for short-lived vendors.

- Also want to confirm: if a subprocessor is activated transiently and is later retained as long-term, what's the contract flow (auto-notice + 30-day objection period, or does it require an amendment)? We should have clear language.

Please see Rachel's draft attached (quoted below). Karen expects procurement input by EOD Wednesday.

—Ben

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karen Holt <karen.holt@bluemarblehealth.com>, BlueMarble Legal <data-privacy@bluemarblehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: telemetry fallback subprocessors — CPRA/annex questions

Thanks for the context — I reviewed Rachel's draft and added language we should propose to BlueMarble. Key points and suggested redlines below (I've put them in plain language for procurement, and attached a tracked draft to the internal drive link):

1) Non-sale covenant: we can accept a limited non-sale covenant for pilot telemetry if we narrow to "Redwood will not sell telemetry-derived identifiers as defined in Exhibit A for the term of the Agreement and for twelve (12) months following termination". We will not accept an indefinite perpetual restriction that prevents legitimate internal research; the 12-month window balances customer expectations and our R&D needs.

2) Emergency activation tiers: propose a two-tier approach — Tier 1 (low-risk, transient caches): self-attestation + minimal security checklist, notification within 48 hours, self-attestation evidence uploaded within 72 hours; Tier 2 (analytics / PII processors): require SOC 2 Type II or equivalent within 72 hours and contractual acceptance of CPRA annex terms prior to processing. This gives us flexibility for truly ephemeral caches while protecting customers.

3) Retention/transition flow: if a transient subprocessor becomes long-term, propose an automatic 30-day notice + customer objection window. If the customer objects, Redwood will halt activation pending a formal amendment. That avoids silent transitions.

4) Evidence & audit: include right to request deletion confirmation and scoped audit evidence for subprocessors handling telemetry. For BlueMarble, we accept KMS-based envelope encryption and will provide key-holding proof on request.

5) Notifications: propose a standard email template (procurement@bluemarblehealth.com; data-privacy@bluemarblehealth.com) + secure link to the transient vendor evidence. We'll commit to the 48-hour initial notice and a 5-business-day follow-up.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm whether product can accept the 2-tier model operationally? Rachel — can you circulate the tracked draft to Karen by EOD tomorrow with the two-tier approach highlighted? Karen — if BlueMarble is OK with these redlines, we can aim to finalize the annex and sign by Friday 2027-09-17.

Attachments: (internal redline saved at https://redwooddrive.company/CPRA/BLM-Annex)

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
